ratings.comment: Definitely a class you can't skip. Lecture slides are posted, but they are missing key details needed for exams. Exam grades are based on an essay question you are given in advance and an analysis of primary sources assigned throughout the semester. Professor Kuby is clearly very passionate about the subject, and overall her lectures are engaging.

The class was manageable overall. Lectures covered a lot of material and focused heavily on discussion of primary sources. Exams were based on those sources and required careful preparation. Other assignments were clearly explained and reasonable in scope.

Attendance is mandatory, but I don't know why because the lectures are so disorganized and random that they don't help on the tests at all. You have to read a lot of primary sources, and the tests are all based on said readings, so lecture content is more of a “I'm making you show up because otherwise no one would.” She NEVER answers emails.
I did not personally enjoy her lectures, but she was heavily respected by many others and the course is well organized.

Professor Kuby is one of the best people that I've ever taken a course with. She makes the lectures interesting and engaging, and is very passionate about what she teaches. She's also great at answering questions, and very helpful. The grading for the course is generous, and it's easy to get an A as long as you attend and keep up with the course.

Prof. Kuby is a very engaging lecturer and clearly loves what she studies and teaches. She makes sure that all assignments have clear instructions (there are regular reading responses throughout the semester and a few small projects) and ensures she is available for questions if we have them.

Super engaging + chill lectures (mandatory). Most content is pretty general + overall themes are important. Tons of reading, but you can get away with skimming or only reading certain ones. Two essays + two exams (neither too bad). TAs grade everything

History 120-
Pros: 
Midterm and final are written, based on readings, graded leniently, and easy to prepare for. 
A few papers, based on readings, which have clear expectations.
Readings are engaging!
Dr. Kuby is very knowledgeable, passionate, and funny so her lectures were great!
Cons: 
I genuinely have none. Take this class if you can!

Dr Kuby's class was one of the best that I have taken so far, by far the best humanities class I have ever been in. She makes lectures very interesting and little to no out of class work besides readings which are usually concise and not too boring, and some small reactions to those readings. Very fair grader.

Professor Kuby is the best. She truly care about her students and makes lectures interesting and engaging. She encourages participation, but doesn't shame or discredit students if they don't want to speak up. She can be a tough grader on papers, but ALWASY gives fabulous feedback that can help you improve for next time.

Dr. Kuby is the best professor that I've ever had. She's amazingly entertaining: her lectures are lively and passionate, and she drives engagement with students without making anyone feel under pressure. I strongly encourage UW students to take any of her classes. She's also passionate about the material, which really makes a student want to learn!

Overall, she was a kind and enthusiastic professor, however, I wouldn't take a class with her again because lectures are very auditory with little helpful information written on slides, which doesn't really work for me. Though the tests were a lot of writing, she provided study guides ahead of time with all the terms/people you need to know.
